text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Bournemouth and Liverpool at the Vitality Stadium.
Bournemouth are one of the form sides in recent weeks in the Premier League, winning four straight top-flight games before a 3-1 defeat to Tottenham.

The Cherries responded to the latter league loss with a 3-2 comeback victory over QPR at Loftus Road to progress to the FA Cup fourth round, in which they host Swansea City on Thursday after this clash.
Liverpool are flying high at the Premier League summit, having lost just once all season to Tottenham back in September after Joel Matip’s late own goal.
The Reds were 2-1 winners against Fulham in their last outing in the first leg of their EFL Cup semi-final, following up a 2-0 victory over Arsenal in the FA Cup third round.
Jurgen Klopp’s side have not played top-flight football since January 1, but were 4-2 winners over Newcastle United at Anfield last time out in the league.
Andoni Iraola opts for three changes to his starting XI from the Tottenham defeat.
Hill comes in for Dango Ouattara, who is away at the Africa Cup of Nations, while Mepham replaces the suspended Marcos Senesi.
Adam Smith also misses out entirely as Aarons starts at right-back.
Former Liverpool forward Solanke leads the line for the Cherries.

Klopp makes four alterations from the win over Newcastle, with Trent Alexander-Arnold and Dominik Szoboszlai out injured, while Wataru Endo and Mohamed Salah are at the Asian Cup and AFCON respectively.
Bradley gets the nod for his first Premier League start, with Elliott, Jota and Mac Allister also returning to the starting XI.
Bournemouth have taken more points from their last eight Premier League games than any other side (19 – W6 D1 L1), while Liverpool rank second for this with 18 points from their last eight (W5 D3).
Who will come out on top here? We’re about to find out as kick-off approaches...
Referee Andy Madley gets this Premier League clash underway!
Great start! Kluivert chops and twists into the Liverpool area before Gomez turns behind for an early Bournemouth corner.
Tavernier and Cook attempt a short routine before the former forces Konate to hook away for another set-piece.
Tavernier takes the direct approach with the second corner but Liverpool scramble clear at the near post.
Solanke then has half a chance inside the area but fails to turn and find a shooting opportunity.
Liverpool have already won at the Vitality Stadium this season, beating Bournemouth 2-1 in the EFL Cup.
The last team to beat the Cherries twice away from home in the same season were Bristol City in 1999-00.
A third Bournemouth corner comes as Sinisterra's dancing feet force Bradley into conceding on the left flank.
Tavernier again goes short before receiving possession back and sending a cross towards the near post that Alisson pushes behind.
Alisson wastes no time to launch a long kick forward, with four Liverpool attackers chasing before Christie calmly heads back to his goalkeeper Neto.
Iraola needs his side to be aware of the counter-attacking dangers the Reds pose with Jota, Diaz and Nunez speeding up top.
Solanke uses his strength to hold Van Dijk out the way before the Liverpool centre-back concedes a free-kick near the halfway line.
The Bournemouth striker will fancy scoring against his old club, and has made a positive start in this one.
The hosts beautifully evade a high Liverpool press but Tavernier's diagonal pass to an unmarked Solanke is poor and Alisson collects.
Iraola's men breezed past their opponents there before the final ball left them wanting more quality.
Jota is perhaps fortunate to escape an early caution after a late challenge on Christie.
Sinisterra then chops past Bradley but runs out of space and the Reds settle for a goal-kick despite their young right-back being exposed there in a one-on-one situation.
Bournemouth have lost all nine of their Premier League games against teams starting the day top of the table, conceding 30 goals and scoring just six.
It’s the most such games any team has played in the competition with a 100 per cent loss record, but the hosts have at least started well here.
Klopp's side have just not been able to make any move click so far.
A sweeping Mac Allister pass releases Nunez but then both Jota and Elliott fail to beat Bournemouth defenders.
Tavernier picks the pocket of Gomez before angling for Sinisterra, who touches inside for Solanke before the Bournemouth striker's control is too heavy and races through to Alisson.
Iraola's men still look the more likely to open the scoring here.
WIDE! Bournemouth invite Mac Allister forward from deep and the midfielder duly obliges, driving towards Neto's goal before drilling a long-range right-footed strike wide to the right.
The Argentina international scuffed his effort slightly there.
Mac Allister's long-range effort was the first attempted shot of this game, such has been the attritional nature of a contest played in windy conditions on the south coast.
The Bournemouth supporters are getting behind their side, but will be slightly concerned after Mepham pulls Jota back to concede a free-kick in a dangerous central position.
Mac Allister clips a delicate free-kick towards the back post but the delivery is too heavy and Konate can only stretch as it goes out for a goal-kick.
Quality remains lacking at the Vitality.
Nunez cuts inside from Konate's diagonal pass but the Liverpool forward hesitates for too long and Christie steps in.
At the other end, Bradley continues to leave space for Sinisterra in behind but Bournemouth are yet to capitalise.
SAVE! Another long-range chance for Liverpool, who play quickly through the lines before Nunez smashes a right-footed drive towards the bottom-right corner.
Neto watches it all the way and makes a routine save, collapsing onto the ball to ensure there is no rebound opportunity.
Hill and Neto fail to communicate as Diaz lurks in behind, forcing the Bournemouth defender to poke out for Liverpool's first corner of the game.
Elliott delivers the right-sided set-piece but Zabarnyi heads away.
A second corner for Liverpool comes in quick succession as Bradley's cross just misses Konate before Mepham bundles behind when under pressure from Nunez.
Elliott lands a well-weighted delivery onto the head of Van Dijk, who fails to make any sort of decent contact.
Diaz is making his 50th Premier League appearance here, becoming the eighth Colombian to reach this landmark in the competition.
It would be hard to know that the Liverpool winger is playing so far, though, as his involvement has been incredibly limited.
Mepham slides across to deny Diaz a crossing opportunity and the ball strikes back off the Liverpool winger to offer the hosts a goal-kick.
The Bournemouth centre-back pairing of Mepham and Zabarnyi have impressed in the opening 30 minutes.
Great feet! Sinisterra evades three or four Liverpool tackles before Konate takes a no-nonsense approach and hooks out for a throw-in.
The Bournemouth momentum abruptly ends, though, as Solanke commits a needless foul near the corner.

Nunez is averaging a goal or assist every 93 minutes in all competitions for Liverpool this season (eight goals, 10 assists in 1667 minutes), with only Salah having a better average for the Reds this term (one every 79).
Nunez’s next goal will be his 100th in his senior career for club and country, though he has had little in the way of opportunities so far.
CHANCE! The Cherries continue to limit Liverpool to only long-range chances as Diaz bursts forward before drilling a low right-footed attempt straight into Neto's hands.
The Bournemouth goalkeeper will not be beaten from that sort of distance.
Play comes to a halt eventually after Kluivert stretches from a challenge with Mac Allister and catches Diaz high on the ankle.
The Liverpool winger stays down and requires medical attention, though the referee and the VAR see no need for further disciplinary action.
It is good news for Liverpool as Diaz is back on his feet and fine to continue, while Jones returns to the pitch after a change of boots.
Can Klopp's men kick on before half-time?
Another fine Konate pass releases Jota, who spins his marker before his low cross just evades Nunez at the near post.
Almost an opening for the Reds, who are in control heading into the break without any reward as of yet.
CLOSE! Fine Bournemouth football creates their first chance of the game.
Tavernier slips a delicate no-look pass for Christie, who cuts inside from the right before blasting a low left-footed effort that Alisson saves in the centre of his goal.
The Cherries look slick in possession.
Good football! Mepham angles a diagonal pass out for Tavernier, whose first-time header back inside is immediately played over the top by Christie.
Kluivert's first effort is blocked on the edge of the Liverpool area before Christie's follow-up shot is again cleared away by Van Dijk.
Iraola gestures to show his unhappiness after Gomez clatters Aarons in an aerial challenge, arriving late and smashing the hosts' right-back to the floor.
The Liverpool defender escapes a caution, however.
It is getting slightly frantic at the Vitality as Elliott smashes into Solanke, leaping into the former Liverpool striker to fell him on the halfway line.
Referee Madley again gives a free-kick to the home side without any further action.
HUGE CHANCE! Zabarnyi clips a fine pass out to Sinisterra, who bursts inside before finding Kluivert.
The Bournemouth winger reaches the byline before his low left-footed cross evades both Christie and Solanke, both of whom fail to make contact at the near post for what looked like a certain goal.
Jota's throughball is behind Diaz, which allows Cook to slice out for a Liverpool corner on the right-hand side.
There will be two minutes to end this half, but can Liverpool capitalise from this set-piece chance?
Elliott's corner is once more an inviting delivery, swinging towards the near post as Konate and Hill contest inside the Bournemouth area.
The ball cannons off the pair and loops over Neto's target for a goal-kick.
HALF-TIME: BOURNEMOUTH 0-0 LIVERPOOL
The half-time whistle sounds on the south coast as Bournemouth and Liverpool remain goalless heading into the break.
Nunez, Mac Allister and Diaz have all tested Neto from range, while Christie went the closest for the home side, who did not have their first shot until the 39th minute.
Kluivert's tackle on Diaz also raised a few questions as to whether the Cherries should still be playing with 11, yet the referee nor the VAR deemed his lunging foul worthy of even a booking.
This is only the second time a Premier League match between Bournemouth and Liverpool has been level at half-time.
The only other time this has happened, the match ended 2-2 in April 2017, the only draw between the two sides in this competition.
Iraola and Klopp will both want much-needed attacking improvements in the second half.

We are back underway at the Vitality! Liverpool have scored in the second half in each of their last five Premier League away games this season, after doing so in just two of their opening five such games – can they keep that run up here?
Bradley's lifted cross is cleared at the back post by Tavernier as Jones lurks in search of a shooting opportunity.
The Liverpool front three must offer more for the visitors in this second period.
GOOOOOOOOOOOOOALLLLLL! 1-0 LIVERPOOL! A huge moment for the Reds, who open the scoring just minutes into the second half.
A lovely passing move from the visitors sees Jota find space on the right-hand side from Jones' offload before the Portugal attacker rolls a pass through for Nunez with his first touch.
The Uruguay forward strides into the area before sliding a first-time, right-footed finish into the bottom-right corner, leaving Neto with no chance.
Jones tees up Jota's clever first-time pass for Nunez to burst into space and open the scoring.
That was a slick passage of play from the visitors.
Kluivert almost responds immediately for Bournemouth as his right-footed strike deflects off Van Dijk but falls the wrong side of the post, going out for a corner that comes to nothing.
Jota has provided 10 assists in the Premier League for Liverpool, with the opening goal being the first he has provided for Nunez, whose strike marks his 100th goal for club and country.
Penalty? Jota continues to be an influential figure in this second half as he drives forward before going down on the edge of the area when under pressure from Cook and Zabarnyi.
The VAR and the referee agree and stick with the original decision of no penalty.

Bradley should score on his first Premier League start! Nunez twists and turns before standing up a lofted cross towards the back post, where Bradley makes a mess of his headed effort and nods wide of the target.
What a moment that would have been for the right-back.
GREAT SAVE! Another opportunity for Bradley in a matter of minutes.
Elliott's left-sided corner is cleared as far as Bradley, whose left-footed shot goes through numerous bodies before Neto stretches to his left to tip away a fine stop.
Kelly returns to action for Bournemouth after missing the last seven games.
The defender replaces the impressive Hill.
Another exciting young talent comes on for the hosts as Scott replaces Sinisterra, likely signalling a move further up the pitch for Christie or a change of formation from Iraola.
Liverpool have won each of their last three Premier League away games, while the Reds last won four in a row on the road in the competition in March 2022.
They have kept two clean sheets in these three wins, as many as their previous 14 away league matches beforehand.
Mepham commits a late foul on Jota in front of the technical area of both managers.
The Bournemouth centre-back knew what he was doing there, leaving a little on the Liverpool forward.
Liverpool are far from happy with Cook, who clips the heels of Bradley from behind before following through to catch the right-back.
The Bournemouth midfielder becomes the first caution of the game.
Solanke, who scored one goal in 21 Premier League appearances for former club Liverpool, has scored in each of his last three home league games (four goals).
He could become the first player to score in four consecutive home appearances in the Premier League for Bournemouth, though the striker has been quiet in this game.
Bournemouth players crowd inside the Liverpool area for a corner but Kluivert's left-footed drive is blocked before Alisson is needed to be called into action.
Down the other end, Elliott makes a mess of a right-sided cross and slices out for a goal-kick.
Klopp uses a stoppage to make a double change, bringing off Diaz on his 50th appearance in the Premier League for Gakpo.
The second of the two changes sees Gravenberch introduced for Elliott, who has again buzzed around the midfield and offered some much-needed defensive support for young team-mate Bradley.
Tavernier has won six of his six attempted tackles, more than any other player on the pitch.

In fact, the most tackles won in a single game this season in the Premier League is seven (Lucas Paqueta v Bournemouth & Neco Williams v Tottenham), meaning Tavernier needs to win just one more to match the 2023-24 record.
Bradley joins Cook in the book after catching Scott with a stray arm in the face near the left-hand touchline.
The Liverpool right-back was far too late to be making that sort of tackle.
Referee Madley races over to have a quiet word with Klopp and one of the Bournemouth coaches after tensions threaten to boil over following Bradley's caution.
The Liverpool manager appeared unimpressed with the decision, while the Cherries were concerned about the challenge on Scott.
Iraola rolls the dice once more as the Bournemouth manager sends on Brooks for Kluivert, who went close earlier in this half with a blocked shot from a left-sided corner.
The Wales winger comes on for his 150th senior appearance.
GOOOOOOOOOOOOALLLLLL! LIVERPOOL MAKE IT 2-0! The Reds have dominated the second half and their reward arrives as the away side double their lead.
Nunez does well up top to hold off the challenge of Zabarnyi, before Gakpo picks up the loose ball and drives forward.
The Netherlands international rolls a delicate pass to his right for Jota, who crashes a first-time right-footed strike in off the near post and past Neto from the right of the area.
Gakpo is immediately involved off the bench, capitalising on some slack Bournemouth defending before teeing up Jota's emphatic finish.
Gakpo dances forward once again before offloading for Bradley, whose chipped cross only finds the hands of Neto.
The Liverpool right-back has impressed on his first Premier League start.
Solanke rues a missed opportunity as he fails to control a zipped pass into his feet, with the ball squirming into the reach of Alisson.
The Bournemouth striker is yet to show his quality against his former side.
Scott's quick feet draw another foul from Bradley on the left flank, allowing the Cherries a chance to send their defenders forward for a wide free-kick.
Cook delivers towards the near post but the ever-reliant Konate heads away the danger.
Great tackle! Konate saves the day for the away side.
Aarons cuts inside, leaving both Gomez and Gakpo in his tracks before opting to pass when the better option may have been to shoot.
Solanke still tries to make a shooting chance from the offload, but Konate slides in with some last-ditch heroics.
OVER! Mac Allister swings a deep right-sided corner towards the penalty spot, where Jones is completely unmarked.
The Liverpool midfielder takes the dropping ball with a first-time strike that sails high over Neto's goal and into the stands.
Van Dijk is tight to Solanke once more, turning behind Tavernier's whipped left-wing delivery for a corner.
Cook delivers the set-piece but Konate rises the highest to thump away a header yet again.
GOOOOOOOOOOOALLLLL! 3-0 TO THE REDS! That is the three points secured for Liverpool as Jota doubles his account and extends the visitors’ lead further.
Nunez bursts down the left flank before his cross flashes across goal and away to the right-hand side.

Bradley recycles possession before his low delivery finds Jota, who wildly swings at a first effort before a fortuitous rebound falls back for the Liverpool forward to drive a right-footed strike into the bottom-left corner.
What a first Premier League start for Bradley.
The young right-back takes the credit for the assist for Jota's second goal, capping a fine performance after replacing Alexander-Arnold in defence.

Jota has scored and assisted in the same match for the third time for Liverpool in the Premier League, all three instances have been on the road (against Bournemouth, Leeds United and Manchester United).
The Portugal attacker has stepped up for his side in Salah’s absence.
Bradley comes off after a remarkable first start in the league.
Fellow youngster Beck is the man to replace the right-back.
Keeping the youthful theme, Klopp also brings off Jones for Clark.
A woeful return against his former side comes to an end for Solanke, who is replaced by Moore.
Seemingly out of the game now, Cook also makes way for Billing in midfield.
Moore is furious with the assistant referee after Liverpool are awarded a goal-kick.
This has been a second-half masterclass from the Reds.
This could be further bad news for Iraola.
Aarons goes down and it looks like it could be his game over.
The Bournemouth right-back has his head in his hands, trudging off towards the touchline holding his hamstring, though he comes back on for the time being.
Beck gets involved off the bench, covering across from right-back to turn behind for a corner to the home side.
Tavernier's delivery looks good but the Liverpool defence once again clear.
Bournemouth will finish this game with 10 men after Aarons is unable to continue.
Iraola has already used all of his chances to make a change, so the Cherries will end a man down after losing their right-back.
WHAT A MISS! That sums up a woeful second half for the hosts.
Brooks is sent through one-on-one with Alisson, attempting to chip the Liverpool goalkeeper but slicing a poor left-footed effort wide to the left of goal.
The Bournemouth winger had to score there.
There will be eight additional minutes to end this Premier League clash, which has been over as a contest since Jota doubled his account to make it 3-0.
GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOALLLLLLL! 4-0 LIVERPOOL! The Reds are well and truly on a roll as Nunez becomes the second forward for the away side to grab a brace.
Mac Allister clips out to the right for Gomez, whose well-weighted delivery finds Nunez at the back post.
The Uruguay forward throws himself at the ball, diverting a first-time left-footed finish in off the right post.
What a game for Klopp’s men.
Gomez gets involved in the act as his right-sided cross picks out Nunez, who does the rest from close range.
A wonderful Jota performance comes to an end as the Liverpool forward is replaced by Gordon.
Klopp appears slightly concerned as Konate goes down holding his ankle following a challenge with Moore.
The Liverpool centre-back should be fine to continue, however.
WIDE! Clark has a shout for a penalty at one end after a lunging tackle from Mepham but the referee waves play on.
Down the other side, Moore races through on goal but slides a right-footed finish from outside the area wide with Alisson stranded.
The Bournemouth striker just needed to hit the target there.
Nunez adds a booking to his two goals after barging through the back of Moore.
The Liverpool striker protests his innocence but referee Madley will not be fooled by his appeals.
FULL-TIME: BOURNEMOUTH 0-4 LIVERPOOL
Liverpool consolidate their position at the Premier League summit after an impressive 4-0 victory over in-form Bournemouth at the Vitality Stadium.

The Reds move five points clear of Manchester City, who have a game in hand, while they are as many clear of Aston Villa and Arsenal in a close-run contest from second down to fourth in the league table.

The visitors were made to be patient in blustery conditions on the south coast, creating little amid a fairly drab first half that was only of interest due to Kluivert escaping a red card for a lunging challenge on Diaz.
Klopp’s men turned on the style in the second period, though, as Nunez opened and closed the scoring either side of a brace for Jota.
Salah’s absence was hardly felt by the visitors, who had Jota, Nunez and a fine cameo appearance from Gakpo to thank for a comfortable victory.

Liverpool stay ahead of the chasing pack before their next Premier League game at Arsenal on February 4, after an EFL Cup semi-final second leg against Fulham and a FA Cup fourth-round clash with Norwich City.
Bournemouth are next against Swansea City in the FA Cup before visiting West Ham on February 1.
That is all for now, until next time! Goodbye and thanks for following.
